payload.headline: Microsoft holds steady: growth and margins improve, but cash flow still lags the price

summary.thesis: Microsoft's sales and profit margins keep improving, but heavy spending has cut free cash flow, so the price only makes sense if that spending pays off.
summary.decision: Hold for the long term; wait on a swing trade until the price reaches a clearer level.

payload.happening: Microsoft closed at 523.0, up 0.36%, in the middle of a sideways range. Cerebras reported a deal with Microsoft, and Outlook was reported down in an outage that also touched AWS and Google users. The next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
payload.business: The core business keeps getting better. Sales grew 18.8% from a year earlier in the latest quarter, up from 18.3% two quarters ago. The operating margin, meaning the share of sales left after running costs, rose to 47.1% from 46.27%. Cash is the weak spot. Trailing free cash flow, the cash left after investment, fell to 60.0B from 78.0B, and the filings note that each dollar invested now earns 30¢ a year against 51¢ three years ago. The reported Cerebras deal fits that spending story: it looks like more AI computing capacity, which adds to costs before it adds to sales. The Outlook outage mainly hurts sentiment and reputation for now. Short outages rarely change demand for core software (general knowledge), unless they keep happening. The balance sheet is safe, with 29.0B in net cash. What's at risk is the payback on the spending, not demand or solvency.

worth.text: The answer depends on whether you value today's cash flow or today's earnings. A cash-flow model (DCF) that starts from the 60.0B of trailing free cash flow gives 184.7 to 296.75 per share, with a base case of 223.82. To justify the current price, that model needs free cash flow to start growing about 41.0% a year, while sales have grown 17–18% and analysts expect earnings to grow 21%. Even 30% growth only gets to 352.37. Against its own history, the stock looks fair. Its price-to-sales ratio is at the 40th percentile of the last five years, which gives a range of 475.73 to 592.92 with a midpoint of 535.43. Earnings multiples are 27.3 times trailing earnings and 21.6 times next year's. Against peers it looks expensive: 11.2 times sales versus a peer median of 4.1. The whole gap between the methods comes from the depressed cash flow. If the spending turns back into cash, the history-based range is the right guide. If it doesn't, the stock is well above fair value.
worth.key_assumption: The heavy spending that cut free cash flow from 78.0B to 60.0B turns back into cash, so earnings (next-year EPS estimate 24.2) rather than today's cash flow are the right basis for value.

bull: Sales growth sped up to 18.8% from 18.3% two quarters ago, so demand is not fading.
The operating margin rose to 47.1% from 46.27%, which means the business keeps more of each sale even while it spends heavily.
Analysts raised next-year EPS to 24.2 from 23.68 over 30 days, a 2.2% upward revision, and the stock is at the 40th percentile of its own five-year price-to-sales range.
bear: Free cash flow fell to 60.0B from 78.0B, and the free-cash-flow margin is just 17.31%.
The price implies free cash flow growing about 41.0% a year, far above the 30% case that is worth 352.37 per share.
At 11.2 times sales against a peer median of 4.1, there is little room for a disappointment.

levels.what: Today's close is inside the fair range of 475.73–535.43, so there's no reason to sell and no safety margin for new money.
The top of the strongest support zone (486.0–491.22, tested 8 times) is where adding becomes more attractive.
The top of the upper resistance zone. Above it, the price nears the own-history high of 592.92, and the case for trimming grows.

longterm.why: The business is improving, but two of three valuation measures lean expensive, mainly because of weak cash flow. Holding fits; adding fits better near 486–491.

swing.why: The price is in its current zone (515.65–524.43), below the flat 20-day average of 529.64 and above the 50-day average of 518.72, so there's no clean edge. A pullback to support at 504.96–512.76 would give a better-defined setup, with resistance at 539.36 as the first target.

decision.timing: Earnings on 2027-01-27 come after the January 15 options expiry, whose implied move of 9.3% doesn't include the report. The free cash flow figure in that report is the main event for both views, so there's no need to rush before it.

change_mind: If trailing free cash flow climbs back toward 78.0B in the 2027-01-27 report, the cash-flow gap narrows and adding becomes easier to justify; a further drop below 60.0B would argue for trimming.
A close below the 486.0 support floor would break the range and weaken the hold case.
If the next-year EPS estimate falls back below 23.68 (its level 30 days ago), the improving-earnings support for the price is gone.
payload.what_changed: The price moved to 523.0 from 521.13, and a Cerebras deal and an Outlook outage were reported, but neither changes free cash flow or valuation, so the hold view and the 475.73–535.43 range stand.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
